name: Humanin
description: Small peptide made by the body, coded in mitochondrial DNA; HNG is a lab-made, more potent variant

status.humanEvidence: Lab or animal only; levels measured in people

items.label: Lifespan
items.detail: Worms; not mice at dose tested

note.text: Human studies only measure humanin in blood or muscle and compare groups, such as children of centenarians.

bullets: **Blocked nerve cell death** from Alzheimer's genes and beta-amyloid (lab)
**Improved insulin sensitivity** when infused into rodent brains
**Lengthened worm life** slightly, depending on the daf-16/FOXO gene
**In people,** the mechanism is not established
Worm, mouse, rat and cell studies since 2001

regulatory.text: Not approved; not on compounding lists
Not named; S0 bans unapproved substances

references: PNAS, humanin protects nerve cells from Alzheimer's-linked damage, May 2001
Aging (Albany NY), humanin in centenarians' children, worms and mice, Jun 2020
